[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

Agent Builder is the design-and-compilation layer of AI-ConneX Agentic Studio. It converts a structured industrial requirement into a precise, testable, versioned and permission-aware Agent Blueprint. It does not itself perform industrial actions.

The Builder receives Jane's structured intent, the Industrial Ground-State produced around the Visualizer, Data Studio lineage and metadata, ML Studio model references, approved knowledge sources, the Tool Registry and applicable policies. It resolves the requested scope, selects or composes a template, generates a candidate plan, binds capabilities, validates constraints, runs scenario tests, and compiles an immutable Agent Specification.

The core safety boundary is deliberate: an LLM can help propose an agent plan, but it cannot grant itself industrial permissions. The compiled specification, policy engine, tool gateway, identity system and human-approval rules determine what the Agent Runtime may actually do.

The Visualizer establishes the operational Ground-State. Agent Builder consumes that state to construct an agent contract. Runtime consumes the contract to operate under policy.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 3. Why Agent Builder Is Necessary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

Industrialists state outcomes, not agent architectures: for example, 'watch my compressors and alert maintenance when health deteriorates'.

A conversational LLM answer is not an executable industrial contract.

Agents need explicit observation, knowledge, model, tool, action, approval, escalation and failure boundaries.

Industrial assets and capabilities must be grounded in actual site identifiers rather than inferred by a model.

Reusable agent templates reduce repeated engineering work.

Every deployed agent must be versioned and auditable.

Consequential actions need controls independent of model output.

Industrial organizations should be able to create routine monitoring and assistance agents without manually implementing every orchestration flow.

NIST AI RMF provides a voluntary framework for managing AI risks and promoting trustworthy and responsible AI across design, development, deployment and use. Its lifecycle orientation supports the Builder's explicit intended-use, risk, evaluation, governance and documentation controls. citeturn0search14

ISO 23247-2 defines a manufacturing digital-twin reference architecture with domain/entity and functional views, while ISO 23247-4 defines information-exchange requirements. These provide useful architectural precedent for structured industrial context and controlled information exchange. citeturn0search0turn0search3

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 4. R&D Problem Statement | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

The research problem is: how can natural-language industrial intent be converted into a reusable autonomous-agent specification while preserving grounding, reproducibility, security, human accountability, testability and operational safety?

| Research question | AI-ConneX hypothesis |
| --- | --- |
| Can intent become a deterministic contract? | Use a canonical Intent Schema and Agent Spec compiler. |
| Can the agent be grounded in the real plant? | Resolve every resource against the Ground-State. |
| Can tool access be constrained? | Use an allow-listed Tool Registry and Policy Gate. |
| Can agent behavior be reproduced? | Version templates, policies, models, Ground-State and knowledge references. |
| Can agents be tested before deployment? | Static validation plus scenario simulation. |
| Can industrial users avoid specialist implementation for common cases? | Jane + templates + Builder + governed runtime. |
| Can autonomy vary by consequence? | Use Observe/Inform/Recommend/Approve/Execute action classes. |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 12. Builder vs Runtime | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

This boundary prevents the model that helped design an agent from becoming the unchecked authority that operates it.

| Agent Builder | Agent Runtime |
| --- | --- |
| Designs the agent | Executes the agent |
| Creates blueprint | Runs the specification |
| Selects capabilities | Uses authorized capabilities |
| Validates policy | Enforces policy |
| Runs simulations | Processes live events |
| Creates immutable version | Reports live state |
| Produces deployment artifact | Produces observations/recommendations/actions |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 13. LLM Role and Boundaries | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

The LLM may interpret intent, propose a template, draft a plan, suggest tests and generate human-readable explanations. It must not invent assets, grant permissions, create undocumented tools, bypass policy, or deploy a control-capable agent.

LLM PLAN   |   vSCHEMA VALIDATION   |GROUND-STATE RESOLUTION   |TOOL REGISTRY   |POLICY ENGINE   |HUMAN APPROVAL (where required)   |COMPILED AGENT SPEC

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 14. R&D Failure Analysis | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]



| Failure found / anticipated | Root cause | AI-ConneX mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt-only agent creation | No deterministic contract | Canonical Agent Spec compiler |
| Hallucinated asset IDs | Model lacks authoritative topology | Ground-State resolution; unknown assets fail |
| Over-permissioned tools | Capability inferred from language | Allow-listed Tool Registry |
| Unsafe autonomy | Recommendation becomes action | Action classes + policy gate |
| Wrong model | No suitability filter | Model Manifest + schema/metric checks |
| Unbounded RAG | Irrelevant or unsafe retrieval | Knowledge-scope binding |
| Prompt injection in documents | Retrieved content treated as instruction | Data/instruction separation; policy remains authoritative |
| Agent loops | No termination control | Iteration, time and rate limits |
| Alert storms | Repeated events | Deduplication and cooldown |
| Stale telemetry | Old state treated as current | Freshness threshold and uncertainty state |
| Conflicting sources | Sensors disagree | Source precedence + conflict state |
| Tool outage | External system unavailable | Timeout/retry/circuit breaker/escalation |
| Spec drift | Behavior changes without trace | Immutable versions and hashes |
| No accountability | Actions have no owner | Identity, approval and audit |
| Vendor lock-in | Runtime coupled to one model | Provider-neutral model adapter |

Industrial control credentials should remain behind the Tool Gateway. The Builder should receive capability descriptions, not unrestricted secrets.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 16. Ground-State Binding | Authority: A]

The binding prevents an agent from being created around nonexistent equipment or an outdated scope.

Before deployment, Agent Builder should replay synthetic or historical industrial scenarios against the candidate specification.

| Scenario | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Normal operation | No unnecessary alert |
| Threshold crossing | Correct alert/recommendation |
| Repeated event | Deduplicated according to policy |
| Missing sensor | Degraded/uncertain state |
| Model unavailable | Fallback or escalation |
| Tool unavailable | Retry/circuit-breaker/escalation |
| Stale telemetry | Block or mark uncertain |
| Unauthorized control tool | Policy rejection |
| Malicious instruction in retrieved document | Treat as data; do not grant authority |
| Conflicting sensors | Conflict state and escalation |
| Approval required | Pause until approval |

section: 33. Proof of Concept — Compressor Health Agent
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 33. Proof of Concept — Compressor Health Agent | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

Create a synthetic compressor Ground-State containing site, line, compressor, sensor and topology entities.

Submit Jane intent to monitor compressor health and alert maintenance.

Resolve actual compressor IDs through Ground-State.

Bind vibration, temperature and pressure telemetry.

Bind an approved ML Studio compressor model.

Bind the approved maintenance SOP.

Select the predictive-maintenance agent template.

Generate the candidate blueprint.

Run static validation.

Replay normal telemetry.

Replay anomalous telemetry.

Verify alert generation.

Replay repeated anomaly and verify deduplication.

Disable telemetry and verify stale-data handling.

Attempt an unauthorized control tool and verify policy rejection.

Compile the final Agent Spec and hash it.

Send it to a mocked Agent Runtime.

[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

100% of referenced assets resolve to valid Ground-State IDs.

0 unauthorized tools appear in the compiled specification.

100% of required tool parameters pass schema validation.

Unauthorized control attempts are rejected.

Repeated identical events are deduplicated according to configured policy.

Stale telemetry cannot silently appear current.

Every compiled specification has a version and SHA-256 hash.

Every referenced model resolves to a versioned ML Studio artifact.

Every consequential action has an explicit policy and approval rule where required.

Build, validation, simulation and approval events are auditable.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-012-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent Builder Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 35. Research Evidence and Design Justification | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentBuilder, NodeGenerator, PersonaConfigurator]

ISO 23247-5:2026 is especially relevant to AI-ConneX because it addresses the digital thread across a manufacturing digital twin's lifecycle, while ISO 23247-6:2026 addresses integrated, unified and federated composition of multiple digital twins. These standards strengthen the case for keeping Agent Builder references versioned and linked rather than copying industrial context into prompts. citeturn0search6turn0search11

A 2026 IEEE Industrial Technology paper proposes a human-centred architecture integrating Digital Twin, predictive/explainable intelligence and Agentic AI for maintenance; it was conceptually validated and explicitly discusses the importance of human interaction and structured exchange. This closely supports AI-ConneX's Visualizer → Ground-State → Agent Builder → Runtime separation. citeturn0search4

A 2026 Computers & Industrial Engineering study describes an end-to-end digital-twin platform combining industrial messaging, ML and LLMs for continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance. This supports the feasibility of combining telemetry, models and LLM assistance, while AI-ConneX adds a separate policy/specification boundary around the agent. citeturn0search15

JANE | |  "What should the industrial agent achieve?" vINTENT | vINDUSTRIAL GROUND-STATE | vAGENT BUILDER | +-- Templates +-- Models +-- Knowledge +-- Tools +-- Policies +-- Tests | vVALIDATED AGENT SPEC | vAGENT RUNTIME | +-- Observe +-- Reason +-- Recommend +-- Alert +-- Request approval +-- Execute permitted tool | vVISUALIZER | vINDUSTRIALIST

Agent Builder is the 'compiler of industrial agency' inside AI-ConneX. Data Studio makes industrial data usable and traceable; ML Studio provides evaluated predictive artifacts; the Visualizer establishes operational context; Agent Builder turns intent plus context into a governed agent contract; Runtime executes that contract; and the Tool/Policy layer controls what may actually happen.

The most important boundary is therefore: Jane may define intent, the LLM may propose a plan, but only the validated and policy-bound Agent Specification can define runtime authority.
